avoid_supplements.name: Anticholinergic herbs (Jimson weed, belladonna)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Direct antagonism of rivastigmine's cholinergic effects; may precipitate acute confusion or loss of drug efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Absolutely contraindicated; counsel patient to avoid all anticholinergic botanicals

avoid_supplements.name: NSAIDs (high-dose chronic use)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Increased risk of GI bleeding due to cholinergic effects on GI motility and increased gastric acid secretion
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid chronic NSAID use; recommend acetaminophen or gastroprotection if NSAIDs necessary

caution_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
caution_supplements.mechanism: Minor additive cholinergic effects; theoretical risk of enhanced GI side effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea; discontinue if GI symptoms worsen

caution_supplements.name: Cholinergic supplements (Huperzine A, phosphatidylserine)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential additive cholinergic activity may increase side effects (nausea, bradycardia, syncope)
caution_supplements.action: Use together cautiously; monitor heart rate and GI tolerance; consider dose adjustment if symptoms emerge

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May delay rivastigmine absorption and reduce peak plasma concentrations; does not affect overall bioavailability significantly
caution_foods.action: Take on consistent schedule (with or without food); counsel consistent timing for optimal efficacy

caution_foods.name: Alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: Alcohol may potentiate cholinergic effects and increase CNS depression; enhances GI irritation risk
caution_foods.action: Counsel moderation or avoidance; assess cognitive and GI tolerance if patient drinks alcohol

monitoring_notes: Rivastigmine undergoes non-CYP ester hydrolysis, minimizing traditional drug-drug interactions, but cholinergic excess remains the primary concern. Monitor for bradycardia, syncope, severe nausea/vomiting, and GI bleeding, particularly in patients on concurrent anticoagulants or with ulcer history.
